newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil seen under pressure.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap - Gas oil seen under pressure.

text.p: Singapore gas oil were under pressure especially for the prompt month late on Monday, which saw buyers staying away in anticipation of lower values, traders said.
"Traders are expecting more gas oil to flow eastwards in July and August from the MidEast as India took very few cargoes in its spot tender for August and its term tender," one trader said.
"That will have an impact on the psychology of refiners and those who have barrels in tankage. We can expect aggressive offers from the refiners before the end of the week."
Traders said the only saving grace to market values would have to come from China. But they said China did not seem keen to buy any more large volumes for the third quarter, they said.
July gas oil was offered at $21.70 per barrel, facing no bids, with $21.65 traded earlier. July was quoted at $21.90/$22.00 on Friday.
August was quoted at $22.10/$22.20, down from Friday's $22.50/$22.60, with deals done at $22.20, $22.25, $22.15 and $22.10 per barrel, brokers said.
Traders said they expect physical gas oil prices could go below $21.75 per barrel when trading starts later in the day.
The gas oil market had moved down on news that Indian Oil Corp bought only 165,000 tonnes of for August delivery compared to 855,000 tonnes it bought for July arrival.
The award was also well below market expectations of about 400,000 tonnes as late as Friday evening, they said.
India also sent more bearish news by cancelling its term tender to buy diesel and kerosene for August 1997-March 1998 delivery.
Traders said India cancelled the tender because none of the diesel offers met its expectations of a discount to spot Middle East quotes.
Shell Singapore's expected lower crude run average for July of 49,000 tonne per day (TPD) compared to its 59,000 TPD capacity is likely to ease the prompt glut slightly, traders said.

But others said more production cuts or a new round of buying are needed to clear out all the prompt physical overhang. Traders said Indonesia might provide some support with its projected five million barrels requirement for August amid refinery shutdowns, but this would be mildly helpful.

The swaps jet/gas oil regrade was steady with July bid at $1.90, and August at $1.70/$1.80 almost unchanged from Friday's $1.60/$1.80. The jet fuel/gas oil spread is steady with July regrade last quoted at $1.80/$2.00 per barrel.
Fuel oil was also unchanged in a flat market with July, August and September swaps quoted at $98.50/$99.50 per tonne, brokers said.
They said there were more buyers on the paper market. On Friday, two buyers--a trader and a major--were said to be supporting the physical market.
